key_insight: The spatiotemporal GNN detects process faults effectively, but its learned attention graphs do not reliably recover physical relationships needed for interpretable diagnosis.
engineering_relevance: Engineers should validate fault-detection performance separately from graph interpretability before using attention weights for root-cause analysis.
method: Model operating-condition-specific normal subspaces linked by transition functions.
Combine GATv2 spatial graph learning with temporal encoding.
Propose reconstruction and Deep SVDD objectives; evaluate foundational components using fault-free training data.
evidence_signal: On the Tennessee Eastman Process benchmark, reconstruction error yielded competitive detection, while attention graphs failed to recover all 22 known physical sensor pairs across multiple hyperparameter configurations.
watch_item: The abstract does not establish the full framework's robustness to changing operating conditions; physics-informed graphs remain a proposed direction for interpretable diagnosis.
paper_title: Spatiotemporal Graph Neural Networks for Fault Detection and Structural Learning in Chemical Processes: Use Case on the Tennessee Eastman Process
